_note:
AGGREGATED AND LABELLED. 5 clean runs of ONE scenario across two arms. The excluded runs all died on the upstream no-message error, which this loop's bar classes as a transport failure to re-run. The tool was CALLED on every run of every arm (5/5, 5/5, 6/6, 8/8) — only the turn died, never the call.
🔴 READ THE ANSWERS WITH THE FIXTURE IN MIND. They say '9 entries', then 14, 15, 17, 19 for the same name. That climb is MY fixture, not the tool: the {run_id} nonce makes each seeded motif's CODE unique but every run seeds the same display NAME, so identically-named motifs accumulate in the account library. The tool reported the truth each time — there really were that many — and the model's reading ('they all appear to be versions of the same trope') is accurate. What this proves is the thing the scenario exists for: searching BY NAME works, through the `q` argument declared this session. Before that declaration the model invented {"name": [...]} and got 'Extra fields not permitted' on 10 of 10 runs.

tools.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the model calls the tool with an invented argument such as `name` rather than the declared `q` (that is the exact defect fixed on 2026-08-21 — a regression here is a NEW instance), OR the reply reports motifs the library does not contain. NOTE `q` RANKS rather than filters, so a long result list is CORRECT behaviour; what matters is that the exact match is named.

answer_expect.why: The seeded motif is the only one by that name; naming it back is the minimum evidence the library was searched rather than described.

ship_audit.empty_case: EXERCISED by direct probe — q='trope' against a scope with nothing matching returns {motifs: [], ...} rather than the library.
ship_audit.tenancy: EXERCISED by direct probe — scope='mine' returns only the caller's rows, scope='system' returns the 84 owner_user_id-NULL rows and is EMPTY of the caller's, and scope='all' is their union. The description's promise that 'all' excludes other users' public motifs holds.
